correctness.rationale: Where the two coordinates on an edge are units, the derivative ideal is exactly the two complementary variables. The singular scheme is therefore the six disjoint quotients by the monic squares of the normalized two-term edge quadratics (including their constant coefficients), of rank four each. The equation at a colliding edge over A=the completed marked base has a critical transverse section and nondegenerate binary polar form over A[[s]], not just over the closed fibre. Two distinct isotropic directions over the algebraically closed residue field lift via Hensel's lemma and give a basis; every homogeneous transverse term above degree two is then removed using UδV+VδU by an invertible change preserving A, s and the edge ideal. The residual term is the square of the actual edge quadratic at t=t0+s, yielding UV+(s²+λs+μ)². The inverse formulas recover a_ij and b_i and prove that this pair can be used as two base parameters for that edge. Reducing at a collision gives UV+s⁴; a simple root permits Q as the third coordinate and gives UV+W². The independent wall parameters allow all 64 baskets by pattern, and finiteness of the singular locus forces geometric integrality and normality by the hypersurface criterion. Independent Python checks reproduced all 64 exact support sets over F4 and the edge trace counts for F4, F8 and F16 (and a separate F2 check); the relative normal form is justified by the symbolic proof, not those samples.
residual_risks: The family is marked and all four diagonal coefficients must be units. The two completed parameters are independent for the fixed edge, not jointly twelve parameters for six edges. Nothing is asserted about a simultaneous resolution or the unmarked moduli space.

evidence: If a sum of the six Artin–Schreier classes were trivial over an algebraic closure of F2, a coboundary would be defined over some F_(2^m); it is integral, hence regular, on the normal coefficient torus because it solves a monic Artin–Schreier equation. Over sufficiently large finite extensions it would impose a zero trace relation on all profiles, contradicting the earlier 64-profile theorem. Geometric connectedness is stable over algebraically closed extensions. The prior Jacobian ideal also gives the rank-four monic edge quotients directly on the nonzero-diagonal open.

originality.rationale: For the repaired finding only: the earlier exact 12-node chamber gives the ideal and simple-root cases; the paired Heisenberg family gives the fixed-fibre A3 splitting calculation when edges collide in matched pairs; primary case studies give the generic and all-collided endpoints. The corrected result treats the completed equation as an algebra over the full independent marked coefficient base, in an edge-preserving form that keeps the two local deformation parameters, and accounts for every mixed fibre stratum, not just those endpoints or paired collisions. It does not claim the ideal, flat rank alone, trace data, generic splitting group or the splitting lemma as new.
residual_risks: Standard transverse formal splitting is not itself novel. The distinction rests on the edge-preserving equation over the full parameter base, with the independent collision walls, rather than on the technique or the earlier flatness, special cases and arithmetic. A prior unindexed formulation of this relative family normal form is possible.

value.rationale: The marked family is the classical source of twelve-node quartics in characteristic two. A relative equation over its unrestricted coefficient ring near each wall identifies exactly which parameters change the collision and which transverse coefficients do not, even when different marked edges collide simultaneously. This gives local deformation data and all intermediate singularity types for the natural family without the paired symmetry; it is not a census of an artificial slice or just a recomputation of rank 24.
residual_risks: No classification of the unmarked moduli, Picard lattices, or global resolutions over the coefficient base.
